correctness.rationale: Independent calculation for A≥1,B≥0: iterated Euler-totient tail H(2^A3^B)=2^(A−1)(3^(B+1)+1)−1, since φ(2^A3^B)=2^A3^(B−1) for B>0 followed by 2^A,2^(A−1),…,1. For n=3^k p with p−1=2^a3^b, φ(n)=2^(a+1)3^(b+k−1), so S(n)=2^a(3^(k+b)+1)−1 and n=2^a3^(k+b)+3^k. Equality iff 2^a−1=3^k. Mod 8: even k yields 2^a≡2 mod8 forcing a=1 and impossible; odd k yields 2^a≡4 mod8 forcing a=2 and k=1. Independent exact totient trajectory comparison for 156 prime/exponent instances confirms the formula; not a proof beyond grid.

value.rationale: The prime predecessor p−1=2^a3^b is the natural zero-extra-prime endpoint of established nested-prime trees in the open classification of perfect totients 3^k p. Uniformly ruling out ALL higher k here closes a structurally motivated infinite subclass and cleanly delineates the known positive k=1 family; it is not an arbitrary numerical slice. Although the final modulo-eight obstruction is short, the explicit tail normalization and rigorous endpoint boundary are needed to compare with published longer-chain results.

final_claim: For p>3 prime with p−1=2^a3^b, a≥1,b≥0, the perfect-totient condition for 3^k p is equivalent to 2^a=3^k+1, hence occurs exactly for (a,k)=(2,1), in which case p=4*3^b+1 prime. In particular no k≥2 member of this smooth-predecessor family is perfect totient.
limitations: Only p−1 3-smooth, p>3; p-1 allowed b=0; no unrestricted k≥4 solution.
Thesis primary full text not read; could affect historical novelty.
